A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Residual Context Diffusion and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Their contents can be reliably matched despite revisions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original RCD accuracy and throughput evaluations, interpolation and training-budget analyses, and the cross-benchmark investigation in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original model evaluations and appendix results, revises SDAR outcomes, and adds initialization and interpolation-ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Algorithm 2 add zero-initialized cold starts alongside reference-model warm starts, allowing inference without a reference model. The entropy-weighted residual construction, two-stage training, and objectives remain unchanged; the new highway-connection terminology describes the existing Equation 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1-Math-220k and OpenMathInstruct-2 for training and retain GSM8K, MATH500, MinervaMath, AIME24/25, and Appendix D's GSM1K/GSM-Plus evaluations. New ablations use existing mathematical tasks rather than extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds evaluated standard-residual (alpha=1) and top-1-token comparison variants. The earlier linear variant is renamed fixed-scalar. The main Chat, SeqD, LLaDA-Base, and Loopholing comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v1 describes warm-start inference, whereas v2 explicitly specifies cold starts for SDAR and warm starts for LLaDA. New Table 5 introduces initialization controls using 1.7B/4B references, the target model, zeros, and a Dirichlet distribution at confidence 0.85. Existing sequence lengths, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 substantially expands validation of key design choices. New Table 5 tests whether reference-model initialization is necessary, finding reference-free alternatives superior, with Dirichlet initialization reaching 77.4% on MATH500. Expanded Figure 5 tests full-distribution residuals against top-1 tokens and alpha=1 weighting. The extended-training and Appendix D analyses already existed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 16-sample Pass@1 for AIME24/25. Neither introduces additional seed or repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Main SDAR results and Figure 4 frontiers are substantially revised. In Table 1, SDAR-8B-b64 AIME24/AIME25 scores change from 15.00/19.79 to 18.75/16.04; AIME25 therefore no longer doubles the 9.79 SeqD baseline. Table 4 and the saturation comparison also change, and new ablation outcomes are added. These revisions accompany changed initialization, so they are not established same-setting gains. Tables 2–3 and Appendix D results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, and Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. Highway connections provide additional conceptual explanation rather than new mathematical reasoning. Neither version contains a changed theorem, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the conversion-budget claim from approximately 1 billion to 300 million tokens, although the one-epoch 300M-token experiment already appeared in v1. The headline accuracy range changes from 5–10 to 4–11 percentage points, and the abstract specifies speedups at the baseline's peak accuracy. The central contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies v1's high-quality warm-start-anchor rationale by arguing that small reference models can mislead initialization. It also interprets the new interpolation failures as evidence for adaptive weighting and full-distribution residuals, and adds a magnitude-mismatch rationale for highway interpolation. Existing contamination and training-saturation interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies alpha=0.3 for the existing fixed-scalar ablation and describes its draft model as untrained. The target-model initialization explanation was already present in v1's Algorithm 1. Appendix C's hyperparameters, hardware information, and the code/model/project links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds two Srivastava et al. highway-network references, Attention Residuals, and Wenke and Fleming on recurrent networks, while removing Press and Wolf. It connects the existing interpolation to highway connections and broadens the discussion's scalability comparison to latent methods and looping transformers. Appendix A remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to initialization, interpolation explanations, quantitative summaries, and discussion passages. Section 4.3 gains named ablation paragraphs, and the preprint footer becomes conference proceedings information. The overall section sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 inserts initialization Table 5 and relocates the former saturation Table 5 as Table 6. Figure 5 becomes a full-width plot with distinct markers, a legend, shaded regions, an expanded horizontal axis, and a longer caption; Figure 4 is replotted. Most tables, diagrams, and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's warm-start-only description, new Table 5 and expanded Figure 5 provide useful tests of initialization dependence and residual design, supporting a simpler inference option and strengthening empirical justification. The gain is limited by an unexplained reporting discrepancy: zero-initialized SDAR-8B-b64 scores 75.6% on MATH500 in Table 5 but 74.4% in Table 1 under nominally matching settings.
